text: Given a valid Calendly Personal Access Token, When calendly_list_event_types is called with no filters, Then it returns a non-empty collection of event types, each with uri, name, duration, scheduling_url
Given active=true, When calendly_list_event_types is called, Then every returned event type has active == true
Given a 31-day start_time/end_time window, When calendly_get_event_type_available_times is called, Then it returns a slot list with no error
Given a 32-day start_time/end_time window, When calendly_get_event_type_available_times is called, Then it returns {error: invalid_argument} and does not call the Calendly API
Given valid credentials, When calendly_get_current_user is called, Then it returns uri, name, email, scheduling_url, current_organization
Given no filters, When calendly_list_scheduled_events is called, Then it returns the user's events newest first
Given status=canceled, When calendly_list_scheduled_events is called, Then every returned event has status == canceled
Given a known event uuid, When calendly_get_scheduled_event is called, Then it returns the full event detail (start/end time, location, status, event type, invitee count)

Given an event uuid that does not belong to the authenticated account, When calendly_get_scheduled_event is called, Then it returns the same not-found/forbidden result Calendly's own API returns for that token (no MSPbots-side cross-tenant mixing)
steps: Connect two different Calendly accounts/tokens (account A, account B)
Get an event uuid belonging to account B
Call calendly_get_scheduled_event with account A's token and account B's event uuid
expect: The tool returns the same not-found/forbidden error Calendly's API itself returns for that token/uuid pair; the service does not return account B's data to account A's token
notes: needs a real vendor account (two Calendly tenants) -- not available to this pipeline; flagged for whoever first connects a live tenant

text: Given a known event uuid, When calendly_list_event_invitees is called, Then each invitee has name, email, status
Given an event uuid and a reason, When calendly_cancel_scheduled_event is called, Then the event is canceled and a following calendly_get_scheduled_event call shows status: canceled
steps: Create or identify a live, not-yet-canceled scheduled event on a real Calendly test account
Call calendly_cancel_scheduled_event with that event's uuid and reason='test cancellation'
Call calendly_get_scheduled_event with the same uuid
expect: The second call returns status: canceled
notes: needs a real vendor account -- write action, cannot be safely run against a mocked or production-shared account; not executed against PROD per the vendor-mcp testcase guidance

text: Given a 7-day start_time/end_time window, When calendly_list_user_busy_times is called, Then it returns busy blocks with no error
Given an 8-day start_time/end_time window, When calendly_list_user_busy_times is called, Then it returns {error: invalid_argument} and does not call the Calendly API
Given an event type uri, When calendly_create_scheduling_link is called, Then it returns a booking_url that resolves to a Calendly booking page for that event type
steps: Identify an event type uri on a real Calendly test account
Open the returned booking_url in a browser
expect: The booking_url resolves (HTTP 200) and shows a Calendly booking page for the given event type
notes: needs a real vendor account -- not available to this pipeline

text: Given the X-Calendly-Api-Key header is absent, When any tool is called, Then it returns {error: unauthorized} naming the missing header, and no outbound call to api.calendly.com is made
Given Calendly returns 429, When a tool is called, Then it returns {error: rate_limited, retryable: true}; given Calendly returns 500, Then it returns {error: upstream_error, retryable: true}
Given two interleaved requests carrying two different tokens, When both call the same tool concurrently, Then each request's outbound call uses only its own token, with no cross-request bleed
Given no credential header, When GET /health is called, Then it returns 200 {"status": "ok"} regardless of Calendly API reachability
